body:
What exists today (src/board.rs:2653)
- serve(top, port) binds tiny_http on 127.0.0.1, which accepts port 0.
- It embeds the board's index.html, fonts and app.js with include_bytes!.
- It exposes the JSON API and an SSE stream at /events.
- It prints the listening URL.
- The frontend is Lustre/Gleam and talks to the server with relative URLs.
- build.rs already builds board/priv/app.js.

The lazy version (about a day)
1. Add a src-tauri/ crate that depends on the solace crate. This means splitting solace-cli into a lib plus bin, or making the Tauri crate a workspace member that calls board::serve.
2. In Tauri setup, spawn serve(top, 0) on a thread and open a window at http://127.0.0.1:<port>.
3. serve currently only prints the bound port, so change it to report the port back, for example through a channel or callback.
4. Set the window's CSP and allowed URLs for that localhost origin. Skip Tauri IPC, since the app doesn't need it.

This keeps one code path. The CLI, the MCP server and the tests keep working, and the board doesn't change.

Things that need a decision or a fix
- Choosing the project root. serve takes the root from the working directory. A GUI launch has no useful working directory, so the app needs a folder picker or a remembered last project. This is the main piece of real work.
- One server per project (.solace/serve.lock, D-230). If the user already has solace serve running, the app fails to start. It should show that as a window message and not a crash.
- serve never returns. It blocks forever and calls println!. On close, the app has to exit the process or add a shutdown flag, because the watcher thread loops forever.
- Agent runs spawn child processes (Claude Code, Codex, MCP, gleam, bun). Tauri doesn't sandbox these, but a GUI launch gets a different PATH than your shell on macOS. Resolve PATH explicitly.
- WebView differences. The webview is WebKitGTK on Linux, WKWebView on macOS and WebView2 on Windows. SSE and the CSS (indigo theme, Plex fonts) should work, but check WebKitGTK on Linux, which is the most likely to differ.
- Build chain. Release builds need gleam and bun first, which build.rs already handles. Add Tauri's bundler and per-OS packaging and signing. Signing is the slow part.

Skip for now
- Replacing HTTP with Tauri commands. It would mean rewriting the API layer for little gain.
- Auto-update and tray icons.

there would eventually be an installer to assist users, then they open the application, and I'd like them to be able to choose where they'd like to access solace either in the browser or the native app.

Design
- The Tauri process owns the server, the same serve() thread as before.
- On launch, the app shows a small start screen:
  - It has a folder picker and a recent-projects list.
  - It has an "Open in: App window / Browser" choice, remembered in app settings.
- App window navigates the webview to http://127.0.0.1:<port>.
- Browser opens that same URL in the default browser with tauri-plugin-opener.
- Both can be open at once. /events already fans out to every SSE client and replays from Last-Event-ID, so two views stay in sync.

What changes because browser mode exists
1. The server must outlive the window. If thcloses the app window, the board dies. Youneed either a tray icon (Tauri supports this) with "Open board" and "Quit", or "closing the window keeps Solace running" as a setting. Browser mode makes the tray a requirement, not an extra.
2. Stable port. Use a preferred fixed port, o bookmarks and the browser's localStorage(theme choice) survive restarts. The picked port should be written next to .solace/serve.lock.
3. Attach, don't fail. With the port in the lock file, a second launch, or a user who already ran solace serve, finds the running server and opens its URL. Thifailure I flagged earlier.
4. Local security. A browser tab means any wnd requests to 127.0.0.1, including the POSTs that start agent runs. I haven't checked whether serve validates Host or Origin. Before shipping browser access, I'd add a per-launch token in the URL, or at least check Host and Origin (this also blocks DNS rebinding). This applies to solace serve today, so it's worth checking regardless.                                               
Installer (later)
- It ships one app bundle with the server inside, plus the solace CLI on PATH for agents and MCP, since agents use solace mcp.
- It registers a launcher entry and optionally a "start at login" tray.
- Nothing in the design above blocks that. It's packaging and signing work.

Order I'd build in
1. Make serve report its port and write it to the lock file.
2. Add the start screen and the app/browser
3. Add the tray and keep-running behavior.
4. Add the Host/Origin/token check.
title: Convert to Tauri
